newsitem.title: ITALY: Unions approve Italian budget but want rate cut.
newsitem.headline: Unions approve Italian budget but want rate cut.

text.p: Italy's three main unions on Monday voiced their approval of the government's 1997 budget, but added that some parts of the bill should be modified and demanded a swift fall in interest rates.

"The budget is fair and will be enough to reach the important goal of entry into European (economic and monetary union)," Sergio Cofferati, the leader of Italy's largest union, the Cgil, told a news conference.
"However we would like a change to the property tax which will mostly hit middle-to-low income families. We will be making alternative proposals to the government," he added.

The government unveiled a tough 62.5 trillion lire deficit-cutting budget on Friday, which it hopes will be enough to guarantee Italy a place among the first wave of countries to form the planned single European currency in 1999.
"A budget of this size has to be accompanied by a strong reduction in interest rates," said Sergio D'Antoni, the leader of Italy's second union, the CISL.

Among measures included in the budget, was a five percent increase in taxes on house and land ownership as well as a five percent increase in the valuations local authorities could base their property taxes on.

Prime Minister Romano Prodi was quoted as saying that he was against the increase in property tax, but added that it had been necessary in the face of opposition from the hard left to Treasury plans to tax people who had taken early retirement. -- Rome newsroom +396 6782501
